summary: Steel lookout tower, 30 m high, built 2003 per provincial data; a 1959 newspaper item says a tower was then planned at Trout Mountain.

events.note: December 1959 Peace River Record Gazette item, quoted by Canada Lookouts, says a fire lookout tower was to be built at Trout Mountain. No source read confirms that it was completed.
Present steel tower, 30 m, per the provincial lookout data

evidence.supports: December 1959 date of the newspaper item
1959 item: building materials moving to Trout Mountain, where a tower is to be built immediately
evidence.quote: Forestry Department is moving lumber, steel and other building materials through the district, en route to Trout Mountain where a fire lookout tower is to be built immediately

evidence.supports: attribution of the item to the Peace River Record Gazette
steel tower, built 2003, 30 m, elevation 795.79 m, active, access mode drive
each site staffed by a lookout observer, generally April to October
evidence.quote: Each site is staffed by a lookout observer whose job is to watch for wildfire all day, each day, generally from April to October.

evidence.supports: sites are isolated; staff must be ready for a wide range of possibilities including a curious bear
evidence.quote: Wildfire lookout sites are isolated and the staff that work them must be prepared for a wide range of possibilities, including an encounter with a curious bear.

sources.title: Wildfire lookouts: Torrens, Vega and Trout Mountain (FRIAA FireSmart vector data, lookout layer query)

notes_for_editor: The 2003 build year and 30 m height match the brief and the provincial record. The 1959 plan comes from a newspaper item quoted secondhand on a fan site; no source read says whether that tower was completed or what became of it, so the story does not say. The brief's access 'closed' is not supported by any source read (the record gives ACCESS_MODE 'drive'), so no access fact is recorded. The brief has no local_unit, so the place is Alberta only.
